solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Return of average rain and mist (6)

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so AV is read backwards

blocks.note: AV is the standard abbreviation for average

explanation.surface: A weather report: middling rain and some mist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all weather, so 'average' looks like a typical rainfall figure; it is only the short form, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour is a fine haze of moisture in the air, which is what mist is.

clue.text: Very current transport minister (5)

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
I is the symbol for electric current
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A description of a lively, up-to-date transport minister in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport minister' reads as one government job, but the phrase splits: 'transport' gives CAR and 'minister' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the church sense: a parish priest ministers to a congregation, not a government department.

clue.text: Urge to fire party lacking skill supported by country (9)

indicators.note: PARTY lacking ART has those letters taken out
in a down answer, the piece on top is supported by the one below it

blocks.note: Romania is a country in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A political party with no talent, propped up by its nation, is under pressure to sack someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urge to fire' looks like pressure to dismiss someone; here it is the compulsion to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is an obsessive urge to start fires.

clue.text: Time at home you put up kitchen cabinet? (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting something up writes it from the bottom, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A DIY question: is it time you fitted that kitchen cupboard while you're home?
explanation.walkthrough: T, IN and U make TINU, which 'put up' turns into UNIT. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a kitchen unit is one sort of unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen unit is a fitted cupboard, so a kitchen cabinet is an example of a unit.

clue.text: Freeze fish which slips under sole? (3,5)

blocks.note: a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Freezing a fish that sits underneath a sole, another flatfish, on the fishmonger's slab.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'sole' the fish; in the definition it is the sole of a foot, which an ice skate is strapped beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skate is a boot blade that glides along the ice beneath the wearer's sole.

clue.text: Lawsuit involving scoundrel falls (7)

indicators.note: CASE involves CAD by wrapping round it

explanation.surface: A court case involving a rogue collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: CAS(CAD)E. 'Falls' reads as a verb for a failing lawsuit, but it is the noun: a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, and falls is another name for one.

clue.text: Tiny child in wartime camp, which slowly grows up? (10)

blocks.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child in a prisoner-of-war camp who will be slow to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is not a container instruction: the camp comes first and the child simply follows it. 'Grows up' is literal, drip by drip from a cave floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite builds up from the cave floor over centuries, so it very slowly grows up.

clue.text: Modify pieces in plug (5)

indicators.note: 'pieces in plug' means the pieces are placed inside the plug, so MEN sits within AD

blocks.note: a plug is a bit of advertising, an ad

explanation.surface: An instruction to change the parts inside an electrical plug.
explanation.walkthrough: A(MEN)D. The surface pictures an electrical plug, but a plug here is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean to make changes, as when a text or a law is altered.

clue.text: Carp I cooked with lime, based on experience (9)

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: carp cooked with lime, a dish the cook knows from experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is CARP I plus LIME; 'with' just adds the lime.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge rests on observation and experience rather than theory.

clue.text: Andean animal of mountain and coastal areas primarily (6)

indicators.note: primarily = taking the first letters of the words before it

blocks.note: first letters of And, Coastal, Areas

explanation.surface: A South American animal found in mountain and coastal regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' reaches back over 'and' as well as 'coastal areas', supplying the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a llama-like animal of the Andes.

clue.text: My face is friendly (7)

blocks.note: 'My!' and 'Cor!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that their face looks friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not possessive but the exclamation 'My!', and so is COR, British slang for 'Gosh!'. Dial is British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: cordial relations are warm ones, from Latin cor, the heart.

clue.text: Phase UK out in radical reorganisation (5-2)

indicators.note: out = not in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to phase Britain out in a sweeping reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' seems to go with 'phase' as in phasing something out; it is the anagram signal for PHASE UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a thorough reorganisation of a body or system.

clue.text: President destroying capital — this is all that’s left? (4)

indicators.note: TRUMP destroys its own capital letter T, which disappears

blocks.note: TRUMP without its first letter, the capital T

explanation.surface: A president has wrecked the capital city, leaving only ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, but it is the capital (first) letter of TRUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is the small remaining part of something larger, as in a rump parliament.

clue.text: Creature a chap found in southern tree (10)

indicators.note: A MAN is found inside ALDER

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Some creature and a man discovered up a tree in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: S + AL(A MAN)DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a lizard-like amphibian, a creature.

clue.text: Undesirable result if feeds etc are modified (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters are modified by being rearranged

explanation.surface: Warning that changing animal feeds and the like could have unwanted results.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'if feeds etc', including 'etc' as three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A side effect is an unintended, usually unwelcome, consequence.

clue.text: Place in play nun is wandering in Hamlet? (9)

indicators.note: letters that wander leave their places, so NUN IS is rearranged
the rearranged letters go in DANE

blocks.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, a Dane

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nun wandering on stage turns up in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: D(UNSIN)ANE. 'Play' suggests Hamlet is the play, but Hamlet is only the Dane; the play is Macbeth, where Dunsinane is Macbeth's castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunsinane is the hill and castle where Macbeth is finally defeated, a place in the play.

clue.text: Disgrace of Republican stopping record change (9)

indicators.note: R stops the gap between DISC and EDIT, like a stopper

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican is shamed for blocking a change to the official record.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'record change' as an edit to an official record; the two words each give their own piece, and the Republican stops the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as nouns: both name the loss of good standing that follows a scandal.

clue.text: Microphone capturing me casually in house? (5)

indicators.note: MIC captures US by holding it inside

blocks.note: in casual British speech 'us' means me, as in 'give us a hand'

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a microphone while lounging around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: M(US)IC. The question mark flags that house is one example of music: the dance genre.
explanation.definitionFit: House is a genre of electronic dance music, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: Heavenly brilliance of bird without name gaining height (9)

indicators.note: STARLING without N drops that letter
the shortened bird gains HT at its end

blocks.note: HT is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A nameless bird soaring higher in a glorious light.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, and only the second N of STARLING goes; HT is added to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlight is the light of stars, a brilliance in the heavens.

clue.text: Slick move by goalie grips United (5)

indicators.note: SAVE grips U, holding it inside

blocks.note: a goalkeeper's job is to make a save
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football report: the goalkeeper pulls off a neat move to hold the ball against United.
explanation.walkthrough: S(U)AVE. 'Slick move' reads as one phrase, but 'Slick' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smoothly polished in manner, i.e. slick.

clue.text: Describe round in combat game (9)

blocks.note: to paint a picture in words is to describe

explanation.surface: Asking someone to recount a round of a fighting game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as a stage of the game, but it is a round thing, a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a mock battle game in which players shoot pellets of paint.

clue.text: Pig’s head on second dish (7)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: A pig's head served as a second course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts P on top of LATTER in the down answer. The surface suggests a roast pig's head on a serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: a platter is one type of dish, the large flat one meat is served on.

clue.text: Bitter about one splitting party — sheer folly (6)

indicators.note: ICY goes about the rest, wrapping round it
to split something is to push into it and part it in two, so I goes between the D and O of DO

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone resentful at one person splitting the party calls it madness.
explanation.walkthrough: D(I)O sits inside I...CY: I(DIO)CY. 'Bitter' reads as resentful, but it means bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name utterly foolish behaviour, and 'sheer' matches the extreme sense.

clue.text: Cut of meat loaf prepared with wine — essential nourishment (10)

indicators.note: a loaf prepared is dough reworked, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a rib is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A meal plan: a cut of meat, bread and wine as the basic diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat loaf' reads as one dish; it breaks after 'meat', and 'loaf prepared' is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Riboflavin is vitamin B2, a nutrient the body needs from food.

clue.text: Thing that helps to contain small elementary particle (5)

indicators.note: BOON contains S inside it

blocks.note: a boon is a blessing, a thing that helps
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Something that helps hold in a tiny particle, like a physics containment device.
explanation.walkthrough: BO(S)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A boson, such as the photon or Higgs boson, is an elementary particle.

clue.text: Hit Friends is returning (4)

indicators.note: PALS returns, going back the way it came

explanation.surface: News that the hit sitcom Friends is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Hit Friends' the TV show; 'Hit' is the definition and 'Friends' gives PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: a slap is a particular hit, one made with the open hand.

clue.text: Composer’s block (5)

blocks.note: an English composer, best known for the hymn tune 'Jerusalem'
a verb from fencing and boxing: to fend off a blow

explanation.surface: A composer suffering from writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's block' reads like writer's block; the 's is 'is', joining two definitions. Sir Hubert Parry set 'Jerusalem' to music.
explanation.definitionFit: One definition by name, a specific English composer; the other a plain synonym from fencing, where you deflect the thrust.

clue.text: A delay when mounting festival (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting means climbing, so the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A hold-up while a festival is being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' looks like staging an event, but here it turns A LAG upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a swimming gala or a gala day is a festive occasion.

clue.text: Son absorbed by proper ancestry (7)

indicators.note: S is soaked up inside DECENT

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son wrapped up in his respectable family background.
explanation.walkthrough: DE(S)CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'of Irish descent' and 'of Irish ancestry' say the same thing.

clue.text: Irritation after Charlie Lake’s silly mistake (7)

indicators.note: ANGER comes after C and L

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a man called Charlie Lake's foolish blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie Lake' looks like a person's name. A clanger is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: to drop a clanger is to make a noisy, embarrassing blunder.

clue.text: Drink can remedy getting tense inside (8)

indicators.note: CURE gets T, taking it in
'getting tense inside' means taking the T into its interior, so it sits within CURE

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Having a drink can cure you when you're feeling tense inside.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN + C(T)URE. 'Can' pretends to be a verb; it is the noun TIN. Tincture is a jokey old word for an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tincture is used humorously in Britain for an alcoholic drink, as in 'fancy a tincture?'

clue.text: Former line in output from bakery (6)

blocks.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An old production line in a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former line' reads as a disused production line; it is PAST + RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry, and the pastries made from it, is what a bakery produces.
